intro: Take our free B1 English mock test to see if your English is ready for Indefinite Leave to Remain or British citizenship. Answer grammar, reading and listening questions, get your score straight away, then practise the speaking tasks out loud.

sections.heading: About this B1 English mock test
sections.text:
Each B1 English mock test has 24 questions in three parts:
- Part 1: 12 grammar and vocabulary questions
- Part 2: two short texts to read, with 3 questions each
- Part 3: two recordings to listen to, with 3 questions each

The recordings are read aloud by your browser, and you can listen twice. At the end you see your score for each part and an explanation for every question you got wrong. Questions are picked at random, so each mock test is different.

Below the test you’ll find speaking tasks with a timer. Speaking is the part most people worry about, so practise these out loud.

sections.heading: Who needs B1 English?
sections.text:
You usually need to prove English at B1 level in speaking and listening when you apply for:
- [Indefinite Leave to Remain](/indefinite-leave-to-remain-ilr/), for example after 5 years on a spouse or Skilled Worker visa
- [British citizenship](/british-citizenship/) by naturalisation

The Home Office has confirmed that the level for settlement will rise to B2 from 26 March 2027. If you’re applying for ILR after that date, try our [B2 English mock test](/b2-english-mock-test/) too.

sections.heading: What B1 level means
sections.text:
B1 is the third of six levels on the Common European Framework of Reference (CEFR), the scale used by the Home Office. At B1 you can:
- understand the main points of clear, everyday speech about work, home and free time
- deal with most situations when travelling, shopping or at the doctor’s
- talk about your experiences, plans and opinions in simple, connected sentences
- give short reasons and explanations

You don’t need perfect grammar. Examiners look for whether you can understand and make yourself understood.

sections.heading: Ways to prove your English
sections.text:
A B1 English mock test is for practice only. To prove your English to the Home Office, you need one of these:
- a pass in a Secure English Language Test (SELT) at B1 or above, from a Home Office approved provider
- a degree taught in English, confirmed by Ecctis if it’s from outside the UK
- nationality of a majority English-speaking country, such as Australia, Canada, Jamaica or the USA

You may not need to prove your English at all if you’re 65 or over, or have a long-term condition that prevents it. See the [official list of approved tests on GOV.UK](https://www.gov.uk/guidance/prove-your-english-language-abilities-with-a-secure-english-language-test-selt).

sections.heading: How to prepare for the speaking test
sections.text:
The real B1 test for settlement and citizenship is usually a short conversation with an examiner. To get ready:
- Talk about yourself, your family, your work and your plans for a few minutes without stopping.
- Practise describing past events, like a holiday or a celebration, using past tenses.
- Give opinions with reasons: “I think… because…”.
- If you don’t understand the examiner, ask them to repeat. That’s allowed and shows good communication.
- Take our B1 English mock test several times and aim for at least 18 out of 24.

faqs.q: Is the B1 English mock test free?
faqs.a: Yes, completely free with no sign-up. Take it as many times as you like.

faqs.q: Is this an official English test?
faqs.a: No. It’s a practice check written by us. For your visa you need a Secure English Language Test from a Home Office approved provider, unless you’re exempt.

faqs.q: What score means I’m at B1?
faqs.a: If you regularly score 18 or more out of 24, you’re likely working at around B1 level. Make sure you practise speaking as well, as that’s part of the real test.

faqs.q: Do I need B1 English for ILR?
faqs.a: For most routes, yes: B1 in speaking and listening. The level is due to rise to B2 for settlement applications from 26 March 2027.

faqs.q: Do I need to pass the Life in the UK test as well?
faqs.a: Yes. Most people applying for ILR or citizenship need both. Try our free [Life in the UK mock test](/life-in-the-uk-mock-test/).

faqs.q: How long is an English test result valid?
faqs.a: A SELT pass is usually valid for 2 years for a new application. Passes used for an earlier successful application can sometimes be reused.
